title: Untrusted input boundaries
outcome: Explain untrusted input boundaries using the deciding step in this fictional service.
scenario: Check shape before permission. A toy tool accepts exactly one ASCII lowercase letter followed by one digit, with no trimming.
given: Inputs h3, H3, h30 and "h3 ". Shape acceptance never grants access by itself.

steps.label: Validate h3
steps.detail: Two characters with the required case and digit pass.

steps.label: Reject wrong shapes
steps.detail: H3 has wrong case; h30 and the trailing-space input have wrong length.

steps.label: Check authority next
steps.detail: An accepted identifier still needs trusted authorisation.

explanation: Input shape and permission answer different questions. Silently normalising these inputs would change the stated contract.

counterfactual.prediction: The shape passes; resource access is still undecided.
counterfactual.reason: Structure contains no evidence of ownership or user permission.

student_task: Classify h3, H3, h30 and the trailing-space input by the stated shape contract. Does a valid z0 grant record access, and which separate gate still remains?
teacher_answer: Two characters with the required case and digit pass. H3 has wrong case; h30 and the trailing-space input have wrong length. An accepted identifier still needs trusted authorisation. Changed case: The shape passes; resource access is still undecided. Structure contains no evidence of ownership or user permission.
project_evidence: For the Grounded Learning Service, retain an annotated trace and the changed-case result. Name the contract or evidence that makes the deciding step valid, so another team can review it.
limits: Some systems normalise inputs explicitly; this fictional contract deliberately does not.
review_note: Individually authored fictional practice, distinct from the reserved independent case. These stipulated records illustrate reasoning; no real service execution or learner outcome is claimed.
